supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS connections in the alert align with the approved DataGrid Analytics updater: dgupdate.exe ran from its installed Program Files directory, and its connections through the proxy went to update.datagrid-analytics.com at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:36 through 14:05 UTC.

Separate from the updater activity, raj.iyer launched C:\Windows\Temp\KB5034441_update.exe with /quiet from Explorer at medium integrity; it ran for about a minute. This does not match the inventory's described IT patching method, but the records do not establish what the executable did.

Cisco AnyConnect's vpnagent.exe started as SYSTEM on WS-RIYER-01. That is notable given the inventory says there is no VPN, but the supplied records do not show it making a connection or establishing a VPN session.

The proxy recorded successful CONNECT tunnels to portal.azure.com, prod-useast-a.online.tableau.com, and aws.amazon.com; those records show user=-, so they do not attribute the requests to a specific process or establish their purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT destinations and tunnel metadata, not the encrypted request contents or specific URLs and files transferred.
The supplied records do not include the KB5034441_update.exe hash, signature status, provenance, or behavior beyond its process start and exit.
The AnyConnect process-start records do not establish whether the client connected to a VPN.
The successful cloud-service CONNECT records do not identify the originating process or the activity performed inside the TLS tunnels.
claims_not_established: The periodic HTTPS connections described in the alert are not shown to be command-and-control or data exfiltration; the available process and destination evidence instead aligns them with the approved updater.
The records do not establish that KB5034441_update.exe was malicious, what it installed or changed, or how it arrived on the workstation.
The records do not establish that AnyConnect was used for remote access or that the Azure, Tableau, or AWS connections involved unapproved storage or malicious activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze KB5034441_update.exe, including its hash, digital signature, file metadata, download or creation provenance, and endpoint detection results.
Collect endpoint process, file, persistence, and network telemetry associated with the executable and its parent process.
Review Cisco AnyConnect configuration and client logs, and check network records for an actual VPN session.
Obtain proxy or TLS inspection metadata sufficient to identify the purpose and process attribution of the cloud-service requests, if available.
Verify with IT and raj.iyer whether the executable and AnyConnect startup were expected.
